chapter: Chicago: Henderson, Tatum and Roy Eldridge, then New York and the army
title: Two years with Art Tatum at the Three Deuces
summary: Collins worked nightly with Tatum in Chicago, made his first recorded solo, absorbed Tatum's voicings, and went to after-hours spots where Tatum introduced him to Billie Holiday.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Yes, yes. The first solo I ever had on a recording was with Art, something called Battery Bounce, I believe. We made the Wee Baby Blues and the Battery Bounce and all this. This was the -- it was unamplified guitar, incidentally, all, But, I worked with Art every night for about two years, and he heard me with my mother's trio. He came by the place I was working, and I wasn't even in the union. And he told me that he had a job for me, to get in the union. So I got in the union, I went to work with him at the Three Deuces. And I said, I had never heard anything like this in my life. Art Tatum would line all the piano players, Alec Templeton, Horowitz, however, they would all come into hear Art Tatum. And the place was crowded, just packed, and they were lined against the wall listening to Art. And I'm sitting here absorbing this for two years, and I had never heard anything -- it just overwhelmed me. And I think I really

started grasping some of it, or knowing what I had learned after I left -- after he left, you know. And I used to play things that I had -- I tried to play some of the things that I heard him playing, voicings and things like that. And this was a tremendous training for me,--you know, just can you imagine. And then after we got off at night we -- in the morning, rather -- at night. When we got off at 4:00 o'clock in the morning then we'd go to an after hours spot.

Me and Tatum and a saxophone player by the name of Scoops Carey. And we'd go and we'd hang out, in an after hours spot. And he'd drink this beer and let every piano player in town play before he sat down. And when he sat down to play he wiped everyone out, you know. But this is --
Did you play with him then (inaudible).

At the after hours, no, I -- then I'd listen, I'd just sit here and listen. As a matter of fact the first time -- he introduced me to Billie Holiday. She came to Chicago to work the Grand Terrace, and we met her, our first night there we met her in the after hours spot and we hung out that morning until about -- that day until about 12:00 o'clock the next day just playing and just having a ball, you know.
